perspective:
Vincent Chinana’s available information:

- He knows he is an Alaska Native man, a mechanic, and long-time friends with Patrick Guzman since their teenage years. They share blue-collar work and have often collaborated, with Vincent contributing mechanical skills and Patrick construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent knew Patrick was considering a new construction venture. He heard Patrick say it seemed like a good opportunity to expand his business, that it was risky but possibly worth it, and that he was still weighing options. Vincent said he had heard it was risky, worried about financial security, advised Patrick to reconsider or delay and gather more information; Patrick thanked him and said he would think it over.
- Over the next few days, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent said they needed to talk, felt Patrick was not telling him everything, and felt betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick said it was complicated, did not want to worry Vincent with details, apologized, admitted he should have been more open, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- During their detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learned the situation was serious. Patrick said it had been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it did not turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses; Patrick thanked him and expressed gratitude.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent said the venture might actually turn a profit after all. Patrick agreed it was starting to look up and said he was relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting him earlier, proposed a joint venture, and said he saw potential. Patrick agreed and suggested working out details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent was optimistic about the joint venture. He said their combined skills could make it a success, proposed starting a business plan and outlining every step carefully. Patrick agreed and said they should cover all bases and set it up for success.
